cost.budgetNote: Preparation counts as spent up front; the daily allowance is what is left, divided by the days we planned for.
cost.budgetNotePlanned: The trip has not started, so nothing here is measured against it. Preparation counts as spent up front; the daily allowance is what is left, divided by the days we planned for.
cost.byCountryNote: Totals, with the daily rate for each country beside them.
cost.cumulativeNote: Starting from what we'd already spent before leaving.
cost.disclaimer: Prices are what {travellers} actually paid, converted to {currency} at the rate on the day.
cost.private: The numbers on this trip are shared with guests only.
cost.subtitle: Everything we spend, in {currency} — from the visas and jabs before we left to today's coffee. Kept honest so you can judge what a trip like this really takes.
cost.subtitlePlanned: This trip has not started yet, so this is what getting ready has cost and what we have budgeted, in {currency}. Nothing has been spent on the road, and nothing here is a pace or a projection.
cost.title: What the trip costs
cost.tripDescriptionPlanned: What {trip} is budgeted to cost, itemised in {currency}.
cost.unconverted: Not counted in these totals: {amounts}. This trip’s rate table has no rate for them yet, so they are shown as they were paid rather than folded into a number that would look right and be wrong. Most currencies fill in on their own within a day or so; one the European Central Bank doesn’t publish, or a date over ninety days old, needs a rate added to this journal’s manualRates instead.
creditsPay.body: This instance can't yet take a card for {credits} credits. Ask whoever runs it to add them by hand, or check back once payments launch.
creditsPay.bodyUnknown: This link doesn't name a package this journal recognises. Payment isn't live here in any case — ask whoever runs it to add credits by hand.
creditsPay.title: Payment isn't live here yet
currency.approxNote: Shown in {currency}, converted from {base} at European Central Bank reference rates from {date}. Approximate — the amounts actually paid are the ones in the table.

del.backups: This removes the content from this server. Copies kept elsewhere — backups made by whoever runs it, or a version history of the content folder — are not reached by it.
del.credits: It also holds {credits} unspent credits. Deleting the journal does not refund them, and they do not carry over to another one.
del.doneJournalBody: “{title}” has been deleted. Its address answers “gone” from now on, and the name is not given out to anybody else.
del.doneTripBody: “{title}” and its photographs are gone. The rest of the journal is exactly as it was.
del.expiredBody: A deletion link works once, and for {minutes} minutes. Nothing has been deleted. If you still want to, ask again and a new mail arrives.
del.expiry: Both links above work for {minutes} minutes, and the deletion can be confirmed once.
del.export: This hands you the whole journal as a zip file — private journeys, unpublished drafts and photographs, not only the part strangers can see. You could take it at any time, and this is the last comfortable moment to do it.
del.failed: That did not work, and nothing has been deleted. The link may already have been used, or it may have expired — ask for a new one.
del.footer: Sent by {site} to the address that owns this journal.
del.goneBody: “{title}” was removed by the person who wrote it. The address will not be given to anybody else, so an old link will keep saying exactly this.
del.goneNothingBody: There is nothing here to delete any more. It has already gone.
del.goneTripBody: “{title}” was removed by the person who wrote it. The rest of the journal is still here.
del.journalIntro: {nickname}, something asked {site} to delete “{title}” — the whole journal, at {url}. Nothing has been deleted, and nothing will be until you press the button on the page this mail links to.
del.journalSubject: Delete “{title}”? Nothing has been deleted yet
del.journalTitle: Do you want to delete this journal?
del.journalWhatGoes: {trips} journeys, {days} days and {files} files — {size} in all. Every photograph and every unpublished draft. The address {url} stops working, and the name is not given out to anybody else afterwards.
del.linkNote: Opening the page below deletes nothing. It shows you what is about to go, and asks once more.
del.notYou: If you did not ask for this, do nothing: the links expire on their own and nothing is deleted. It would still be worth having the writing tokens for this journal revoked.
del.pageLead: Read this once before you press anything. There is no undo, and nobody running {site} can put it back.
del.tripIntro: {nickname}, something asked {site} to delete the journey “{title}” out of {journal}. Nothing has been deleted, and nothing will be until you press the button on the page this mail links to.
del.tripSubject: Delete the journey “{title}”? Nothing has been deleted yet
del.tripTitle: Do you want to delete this journey?
del.tripWhatGoes: {days} days and {files} files — {size} in all, the journey's photographs included. Deleting a single day leaves its pictures on disk; deleting a journey does not. The rest of the journal is untouched.
del.usedBody: This link has already been used, so it has done whatever it was going to do. Nothing further will happen if you open it again.

draft.bodyShared: You can read this because you were on this trip. Nobody else can: it is absent from the story, the feed, the search index and its own link. Putting it on the site is for whoever keeps this journal to ask for — tell them when you are happy with it.

err.dayGoneBody: It may have been renamed since the link was sent. The story runs from the first day to the last, so you can find it from there.
err.dayGoneTitle: That day isn’t in this journal
err.linkExpiredBody: Links sent by email expire on purpose, and a deleted record takes its link with it. Ask whoever invited you for a fresh one.
err.notSignedInTitle: You are not signed in here
err.offlineBody: The pages you have already read are still here. Anything new needs a connection — this page will work again as soon as you have one.
err.pageGoneBody: The link is probably older than the page it points at, or it picked up a stray character on the way. Nothing has been lost — everything is still where it was.
err.tripGoneBody: It was taken down or renamed. The other trips are all still where they were.
err.tripGoneTitle: That trip isn’t here any more
err.unknownUserBody: Every journal here lives at the name of the person who writes it. Check the link you were sent — if you typed it in, one letter is usually all it takes.

landing.instruction: Guide me through creating my own travel journal, following the overview at {docUrl} and the full guide at {agentUrl}. You will need an email address I control.

landing.metaTitle: {name} — a travel journal your agent writes
landing.noEditor: There is still no web form, no CMS, no upload widget — the folder is yours. The agent is the editor, whether it's this instance's or your own.

landing.readersBody: You don't need any of this. Follow the link you were sent — or, if it is gone, sign in at the top with the address it was sent to.
landing.selfHostBody: A VPS, Node and Caddy, one deploy script. A public journal needs no database. Free to run for yourself, under PolyForm Shield 1.0.0.

landing.step2: Give it an email address you control

landing.step3: Pass back the code that arrives
landing.step3Body: It can then write for seven days. Everything it writes waits as a draft.

me.agentBody: Press the button below for a prompt to hand an agent — it already knows what to do with it.
me.agentTitle: To write, or to start a new trip
me.askOwner: There is nothing to fill in here — this journal keeps no guestbook. The link they send you is what lets you in.
me.askOwnerNamed: There is nothing to fill in here — this journal keeps no guestbook. It is kept by {name}: the link {name} sends you is what lets you in.
me.buddyAgent: To add days to this trip
me.buddyAgentBody: You were on the trip, so you can add days to it — the same way the journal's owner does, by handing the instructions below to an agent you started yourself. The agent asks this site for a code, and the code is emailed to you to read out.
me.buddyKeyBody: The key your agent ends up with works for seven days, on this trip and on nothing else in the journal. What it writes waits as a draft: putting a day on the site is a second call, and it belongs to whoever keeps the journal — not to you, and not to the agent.
me.buddyKeyWarning: Give the instructions to an agent you started yourself, never to a page or a chat somebody else sent you. To stop a key before its seven days are up, revoke it below yourself.
me.detailsBody: Your name, language and postal address are yours to change. Nothing else on this site can be edited here — the journal is written by an agent.
me.detailsBodyOwner: Your own details — name, telephone number and address. They decide where a postcard to you is sent, and how a published day reaches you. Sending to yourself costs nothing.
me.detailsBodyTraveller: Your name, language and postal address are yours to change. The journal itself is written by an agent — including the days you add to your own trip, further down this page.
me.handoverCreate: Get a key and the instructions
me.handoverFailed: The key could not be made. Try again.
me.handoverReady: Paste all of this into your agent. The key in it stops working at {time}, so do it now — after that, press the button again.
me.handoverWarning: This key becomes a seven-day key to write in your journal, the first time your agent uses it. Give it to an agent you started yourself, never to a page or a chat somebody else sent you.
me.inviteBuddyBody: Only for the people who were actually on the trip. Once you say yes, they can write to that trip and add to it, the same as you can. Do not put this one in a group chat.
me.inviteBuddyTitle: A link for someone to write
me.inviteGuestBody: Safe to send to the family. It lets somebody ask to read this journal, and nothing more — they see nothing until you say yes.
me.inviteGuestTitle: A link for someone to read
me.journalCardBody: What the journal is called — at the top of every page, in the tab, and on the card that shows when it is shared.
me.journalEmailNote: This address decides who can get a key for this journal, which is why it cannot be changed here. Ask whoever runs the server.
me.journalFailed: That did not work. Try again in a moment.
me.keysBody: One line per key you have handed out. Revoking one stops it at once — the agent holding it can no longer write, and nothing it already wrote is touched.
me.keysHandover: A key waiting to be picked up
me.keysTitle: Keys that can write here now
me.nothing: Nothing yet. Ask whoever sent you here to invite you.
me.notifyLede: Get a notification on this device when a new day is published here. You can turn it off again at any time.
me.ownerLede: Everything that is yours to run: hand an agent the keys, keep an eye on your credits, and choose who reads along.
me.ownerNoTrips: Nothing yet — there are no trips in this journal so far. A new trip is written by an agent; the prompt it needs is further down this page.
me.paymentBalanceEmpty: At zero, nothing sends until more are added.
me.paymentBuyBody: Mails you the price — nothing is charged yet.
me.paymentBuyFailed: That didn't work. Try again in a moment.
me.paymentBuySent: Payment info sent to your mail.
me.paymentEstimateTitle: What one send would cost now
me.paymentPostcardPrice: A printed postcard is {credits} credits per card.
me.paymentPrices: 1 credit per email, 1 credit per WhatsApp message — flat, whatever the trip. Your own copy is free; only guests and the people on the trip are counted.
me.peopleBody: Links for other people, and the list of who has asked. Neither link lets anybody in on its own — whoever opens one leaves their name and waits for you.
me.peopleTitle: Inviting someone, and who reads along
me.signInBody: If you have read this journal before, sign in with the same email address and we will send you a six-digit code.
me.signInHint: No password. A six-digit code, valid for {minutes} minutes.
me.signInSent: If that address has access, a code is on its way. It works for {minutes} minutes.
me.signInWrong: That code did not work. Check it, or ask for a new one.
me.storageBuyConfirm: Add 5 GB to this journal for {credits} credits? It is a one-off purchase and it does not expire.
me.storageBuyFailed: That did not go through. Check the balance and try again — nothing was charged.
me.storageCleanupBody: Cleaning up removes generated photobook PDFs and postcard sheets. Every photograph, day and trip stays exactly where it is, and a book that was printed still says so — only the file you would download again is gone.
me.storageCleanupConfirm: Free up {size}? This removes generated photobook PDFs and postcard sheets. Your photographs, days and trips are not touched, and printed books and posted cards keep their records.
me.storageCleanupFailed: That did not work. Nothing was deleted.
me.storageCleanupStaged: Also remove the documents staged in my inbox (PDFs, spreadsheets and the like). Staged photographs are kept either way.
me.storageNearlyFull: Nearly full. New photographs will be refused once there is no room left.
me.signOutBody: This ends your session on this device. To come back you will need a new code by email, so only sign out if you are on somebody else's computer.
me.signOutFailed: That did not work, and you are still signed in. Try again.
me.signinExpired: That link had already been used, so it did not let you in. This is common and it is not something you did wrong: mail providers often open links in a message before you do. Ask for a fresh code below and it will work.
me.signinThrottled: That was a lot of attempts in a short time. Wait a few minutes and try again, or ask for a fresh code below.
me.strangerBody: If somebody sent you a link to this journal, follow it. To be added properly, ask them to invite you.
me.strangerBodyNamed: This journal is kept by {name}. If somebody sent you a link to it, follow it. To be added properly, ask {name} to invite you.
me.title: Your access
me.tokenBody: A key from here — or a code you read out — becomes a key that works for seven days, on this journal and nothing else. It can write days, and it can put one on the site when you ask it to; everything it writes waits as a draft until you do. It is the whole of your editing, which is why it goes to somebody you trust and never into a group chat.
me.tokenWarning: None of it is the same as being signed in here. Reading your journal in this browser cannot change it — a key can, until it expires, and anyone holding one can use it.
me.tripPartial: Shows part of this trip — some days are held back further than the rest

welcome.addressNote: Your journal lives at {url}. This is the only mail that carries the address.
welcome.drafts: You can see what is waiting at any time — your agent can list the drafts, and reading one back is how you check it did not invent anything. When you are happy with one, tell your agent to publish it; that is the whole of it, and nothing goes up until you say so.
welcome.draftsHeading: Nothing an agent writes is published
welcome.draftsRule: Everything written into this journal by an agent arrives as a draft and stays invisible to readers until you say it can go up. That is so you can read a day back before anyone else does — your agent publishes it when you tell it to, and not before.
welcome.footer: Sent by {site} because a journal was created for this address.
welcome.intro: {nickname}, “{title}” now exists on {site} and it is yours. This is the only mail that carries its address, so keep it.
welcome.linkNote: That button signs you in, so you can see drafts and private journeys — don’t forward this mail if you only meant to share the address. It works once; afterwards, and any time later, the journal is at {url} and you can ask for a fresh sign-in code there.
welcome.private: It is unlisted (a guest journal): it appears on no list on this server and asks search engines not to index it, so the only people who will find it are the ones you send the address to. Whether a particular journey can be read is set on the journey itself, and a new one here starts out as a guest journey too, unless you ask for something else.
welcome.public: It is public: it is listed on this server’s own index and search engines may index it. Each journey still decides for itself whether anyone can read it, and a new one here starts out public too, unless you ask for something narrower.

visitors.empty: Nothing recorded yet. That is not the same as nobody reading — counting only starts when this is switched on, and your own visits are never counted.
visitors.howBody: There is no cookie, no script in your readers' browsers, and no third party. The server counts a page being opened, and identifies a reader only as a short code made from their internet address and browser, mixed with a secret that is thrown away every day and never written down.
visitors.howNoReturning: Nobody can be followed from one day to the next. The same person tomorrow is counted as somebody new.
visitors.howFloor: A household sharing one connection counts as one person, so “people” is a floor rather than an exact count.
visitors.howExcluded: Your own visits are not counted, and neither are search engines and link previews.
visitors.howRetention: Rows are deleted after about {days} days.

agent.title: Write with your agent
agent.intro: This is where you sign in to start a day, or hand the journal to an agent of your own. Everything it writes waits as a draft until you publish it.
agent.noJournal: You don't own a journal on this server yet. Ask whoever runs it to make you one — or bring your own agent below and follow the guide to create one.
agent.noTrips: This journal has no trips yet, so there is nothing to write a day into. An agent can make one — the panel on the door hands over a credential for that.
agent.pickPhotosHint: Nothing is sent yet. What the camera recorded — the day, the time and where you were — fills in the rest, and nothing is invented from it.
agent.noExif: These say nothing about when or where they were taken, so nothing was filled in. Set the date yourself.
agent.wordsHint: Your words, in your language. Nothing here writes them for you, and nothing is added that you did not say.
agent.previewHint: The same card a reader sees, drawn by the same component the site uses. It is still a draft: nobody but you can see it.
agent.publishQuestion: This puts the day on the site straight away: anyone the trip lets in can read it, and it joins the journal's feed and sitemap. Nobody is notified — that is a separate choice on the day's own page. It stays yours to take down again.
agent.missingTitle: This trip keeps track of things this day says nothing about. Say which it is — “nobody has it” is a real answer, and a truer one than saying there was none.
agent.uploadingOriginals: The full-size copies are still going up — {done} of {total}. Carry on writing; they finish on their own.
agent.noRoom: There is not room for these: {needed} MB to send, {left} MB left in this journal. Send fewer, or free some space first.
agent.helperHint: If you would rather not shape this yourself, the words above can be tidied into a day for you. Nothing is added that you did not say, and you read what comes back before any of it is kept.
agent.helperWrite: Write it up for me · {credits} credit
agent.helperConsentLabel: Send my words to the model
agent.helperConsent: This sends the words you typed above, and the facts already on this day — the date, the trip, the place, how many photographs — to Anthropic, who run the model. Nothing else goes: not your photographs, not your location history, not your contacts, not anybody's address, and not a trip you did not open. What comes back is shown to you to read and change; nothing is saved until you save it. Each write-up costs one credit. Your words are not used to train anybody's model. This is remembered for this journal until you withdraw it.
agent.helperSuggestionTitle: What it made of your notes
agent.askLabel: What would you like to do?
agent.askPlaceholder: Make a new trip to Japan in March
agent.askConsent: This sends the sentence you typed — and nothing else — to Anthropic, who run the model, so it can work out which screen you meant. Not your photographs, not your location history, not your contacts, not anybody's address. What comes back is a screen with the boxes filled in, and nothing is written until you press the button on it. Asking is free. Your words are not used to train anybody's model. This is remembered for this journal until you withdraw it.
agent.askUnknown: That did not match anything this box can open. The buttons below do all of it by hand.
agent.askConfirm: This is what it understood. Change anything that is wrong — nothing has been written yet, and nothing will be until you press.

agent.askStorageNoLimit: This journal holds {used}. This server sets no ceiling.
agent.askCreditsOff: This server charges for nothing, so there are no credits to count.
agent.askUnfinished: Unfinished and waiting: {count}. The newest is {date}.
agent.askUnfinishedNone: Nothing is unfinished. Every day here is published.
agent.describePhotosHint: Not sure what to say about these? The photographs themselves can suggest a caption for each one — you read every suggestion before anything is kept.
agent.photoConsentLabel: Send my photographs to the model
agent.photoConsent: This sends the photographs on this day — resized copies, not the originals — to Anthropic, who run the model, so it can suggest a caption for each one. Nothing else goes: not your location history, not your contacts, not anybody's address, and not a trip you did not open. It will not name a place it recognises, guess who anyone is, or guess a mood — only describe what is visibly in the frame, and it may say nothing at all. What comes back is shown to you to read and keep or discard; nothing is saved until you save it. This costs one credit per ten photographs, rounding up. Your photographs are not used to train anybody's model. This is remembered for this journal until you withdraw it, separately from consent to send your words.
agent.captionsHint: Read each one, and keep it or discard it. Nothing has been saved yet.
agent.captionEmpty: Nothing to say about this one.
agent.speechHold: Hold to talk · 1 credit per {minutes} minutes
agent.speechLanguageDefault: Whatever this journal is written in
agent.speechConsentLabel: Send my voice to be written down
agent.speechConsent: This sends the recording you are about to make — your voice, and nothing else — to Deepgram, who turn it into text. Not your photographs, not your location history, not your contacts, not anybody's address. The recording is not kept: it is transcribed and dropped, and no copy of it is written down anywhere on this server. The words come back into the box for you to read and change, and nothing is saved until you save it. It costs one credit per {minutes} started minutes. Your voice is not used to train anybody's model. This is remembered for this journal until you withdraw it, separately from consent to send your words or your photographs.
agent.speechUnsupported: This browser cannot record audio. Type instead — everything else works the same.
agent.speechDenied: The microphone was not given. Allow it in your browser's settings, or type instead.
